claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements.
The target alloys are equilibrium, single-phase materials with quantifiable local chemical disorder.
The proposed approach couples DFT-calculated phonon properties to regression models using compositional and disorder descriptors.
The integrated DFT and machine-learning approach will predict low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional phenomenological and standard ab initio models.
Chemical short-range order and atomic-scale disorder enhance phonon scattering.
DFT can capture the effects of local chemical environments on phonon lifetimes.
Embedding DFT-derived local-environment effects in a machine-learning model accounts for disorder-induced phonon scattering.
Conventional averaging models overlook disorder-induced phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Phonon transport dominates thermal conductivity in the relevant mid- to high-temperature regime.
The proposed approach will reduce predictive error by at least 20–30% relative to established models.
Alloys identified as low-conductivity candidates will exhibit significantly reduced phonon transport experimentally.
The method is applicable only within a specified compositional subset and temperature regime for which disorder is well characterized.
The method may not be reliable for phase-segregated alloys, alloys undergoing ordering transitions, or alloys produced under non-equilibrium conditions.
TDTR will be used to measure phonon thermal conductivity across the relevant temperature range.
Chemical short-range order will be characterized to confirm the expected disorder state.
Prediction-error metrics for the proposed and conventional models will be compared on synthesized high-entropy alloys.

The hypothesis will be falsified if the approach achieves less than approximately a 20% reduction in predictive error or if predicted low-conductivity alloys do not experimentally show low conductivity.
